text:
1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system, the app shell and the architecture as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*

1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal),
10	`/f/:project/cleanup` (Clean up, modal), `/f/:project/branches/:branch/discard`
11	(Discard a branch, modal), `/f/:project/app/koda` (Upgrade Koda, modal).
12	Fragments: `/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical
13	(spark-lending), new project, app being built, update clashed (with the app
14	on the shell's branch and a failed push), long names (an existing app to
15	connect, no remote), large project (a hundred features), Koda behind, Koda
16	upgrading, Koda to install. Also `/f/:project/app/koda/install` (modal).
17	
18	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
19	
20	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
21	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
22	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
23	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
24	   split).
25	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
26	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
27	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
28	   real app opens the new design's page).
29	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
30	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
31	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
32	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also

1	# The agent follows the app's own Koda, and Prelude installs it only with the person's approval
2	status: proposed
3	date: 2026-10-23
4	parts: designs, pages, installs, server, agent, host, branches
5	
6	## Context
7	Every prompt points the agent at Prelude's own installed Koda (`server/main.js` resolves `@kodalang/core`), so an app on another version gets guidance for attributes it doesn't have. Upgrading an app's Koda needs `npm install`, which the agent can't run and nothing in Prelude does. `node_modules` isn't in git, so a fresh worktree has none, and merging an upgrade leaves the old Koda installed in the person's checkout.
8	
9	## Decision
10	`designs` finds the app's Koda and reads its version from `node_modules/@kodalang/core/package.json`: first in the worktree (the app's path from `prelude.json`, then the root), then the same in the project's own checkout, and Prelude's only when neither has one. It also reads the version the app's `package.json` asks for. The server passes the Koda it found to every prompt as `kodaPath` and to `--add-dir`, and the design host serves its runtime to a design's pages (`/_prelude/koda/`), so designs behave as the app will; Prelude's own pages keep Prelude's.
11	
12	`pages` compares the app's version with Prelude's on the project page and offers an upgrade, which starts a fix. A new part, `installs`, runs the project's package manager (chosen by its lockfile) in two places: in that fix's worktree, installing Prelude's version, and in the person's checkout once the upgrade is merged, installing the version `package.json` asks for. `pages` offers that second install when the checkout's installed Koda isn't the one it asks for. Either way the command is fixed (never one the agent wrote), names only `@kodalang/core`, has a time limit, and runs only after the person approves it, seeing it first, as with a host: install scripts are code from outside the project.
13	
14	## Consequences
15	The agent, the designs and the app all use

I've built the Koda change to Project, but nothing has run yet; Prelude's render check after this turn is the first test. Two things differ from the design, and the person should look at those before approving the screens.

**Views** (`server/views/projects/`)
- `page.eta` was already identical to the design's version, so I didn't change it.
- `_app.eta` now has the design's Koda block: the line saying the app's Koda is behind, with Upgrade Koda…, or a link to the upgrade already under way. Below that sits the install-in-your-folder line, which also shows installing and failed.
- `_koda.eta` and `_koda-install.eta` are new and copied element for element. The one exception: the upgrade form's hidden `upgradeBranch`/`upgradeUrl` fields are gone, because they only stood in for the fix name the app now makes itself.
- No style changes were needed.
- In `routes.json` every view points at `@app/server/views/...`, and both `"from"` entries are removed.

**Model and server**
- **Reading the versions:** `kodaOf()` in `server/app-config.js` reads which Koda is installed in the app's folder and which version its `package.json` asks for.
- **The card's data:** `kodaModel()` in `server/project.js` fills `app.koda`, comparing against Prelude's own Koda version.
- **The upgrade is never offered twice:** not while one is already under way, and not while a merged one is still waiting to be installed in your folder.
- **New file `server/installs.js`:** this is the `installs` part that the existing decision D-k7v describes but nobody had built. It picks npm, pnpm or yarn from the lockfile, builds every command itself, stops after 5 minutes, and keeps the end of the output if the install fails.
- **Upgrade Koda:** clicking it creates the fix "Upgrade Koda to x.y.z" on its own branch. It runs the exact command the modal showed, only in that fix's copy of the project. When the install finishes it starts the agent's first turn there. If that copy would need a different command, nothing runs.
- **Install Koda:** runs only in your own folder, only after you confirm in the modal. The card refreshes when it finishes.
- Each POST closes the modal and refreshes the app card. If the request is refused, the modal comes back and says why.

R-k2d, R-q7w and R-n6t are no longer marked proposed in RULES.md. Everything stays within the parts the architecture allows, so I didn't propose a new decision. `project.js` reaches the installs through the app object, the same way it already reaches the app runner.

**Check before approving and opening the PR** (all written up in NOTES.md):
1. **Install command in your folder:** it's `npm install --no-save @kodalang/core@<version>`, or `pnpm`/`yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, not the design's plain `npm install @kodalang/core@…`. The plain command would rewrite `package.json` and the lockfile, which breaks the modal's promise that only `node_modules` changes.
2. **After clicking Upgrade Koda**, the modal closes and the card links to the fix, as `routes.json` says, instead of opening the fix's page. The fix has nothing to show until its install ends.
3. **The fix's branch** is named `prelude/fix-upgrade-koda-to-0-1-5`, because that's how the app names fix branches. The design shows `prelude/fixes/…`.
4. **`node_modules` in the fix:** the fix's turns commit everything in its folder, as every branch's do. An app that doesn't ignore `node_modules` in git would get it committed on the fix branch.
5. **Not built:** the rest of D-k7v is outside this design, namely giving the agent the app's own Koda instead of Prelude's, and the design host serving it. The upgrade's own turn is unaffected, since the version it upgrades to is Prelude's own.

For the screens: typical, new-project, app-being-built, update-clashed, long-names and large-project should render as before, with no Koda line on the card. The new Koda line and modals show in koda-behind, koda-upgrading and koda-to-install.
